GOLDMAN SACHS
SUMMER ANALYST INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
YEAR - 2024
SNEHA MENAT
COMPUTER ENGINEERING
BATCH - 2026

Online Assessment (OA)
Platform - Hackerank (Video and Screen proctored)
The online assessment consisted of:
●
10 multiple-choice questions (MCQs) -15 mins
●
3 coding questions - 40 mins
●
1 HR-related questions - 5mins
As much as I remember, we were allocated 55 minutes to complete the MCQs and
coding questions, and an additional 5 minutes for the HR questions. Each MCQ earns
you 3 marks for correct answer and -1 mark for incorrect answer.
Coding Questions - 3 Questions
1) Modest Number
The problem is to identify modest numbers within a given range (inclusive of start
and end). A number is considered modest if it can be split into two parts (left and
right), such that dividing the number by the right part gives a remainder equal to the
left part. The program should check all possible combinations of left and right
partitions of a number to verify this condition.
Solution Approach
1.
Splitting Numbers: Iterate over all digits of a number to partition it into left and
right parts.
2.
Validation: Check if the right part is non-zero and if the condition number %
right == left holds.
3.
Iterate Over Range: For every number in the given range, apply the above
check.
4. Output: Collect and print all numbers that satisfy the modest number
property.
2

This approach ensures all possible partitions are tested for each number within the
range.
2) Identifying Unique Colors on Painting Sheets
Problem:
You are given N rectangular painting sheets and M shots. Each sheet is defined by
four integers representing the bottom-left and top-right corners of the rectangle, i.e.,
(x1, y1) and (x2, y2). Each shot has a set of coordinates (x, y) and a color. The goal is to
determine, for each sheet, how many unique colors have been shot within the
boundaries of that sheet.
●
For each shot, you need to check if the shot's coordinates lie within the bounds
of each painting sheet.
●
If the shot is within a sheet, the color of that shot should be considered for that
sheet.
Input:
●
N (number of painting sheets) and M (number of shots).
●
N rectangles, each defined by four integers (x1, y1, x2, y2), representing the
coordinates of the bottom-left and top-right corners.
●
M shots, each defined by three integers: (x, y) for the coordinates and color
for the color of the shot.
Output:
●
For each sheet, output the number of unique colors that have been shot within
the sheet's bounds.
Solution Approach:
3

1.
Store Sheet Data: Each sheet is represented by a rectangle with four
coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2).
2.
Track Unique Colors: For each shot, check if the shot’s coordinates fall within
the bounds of each sheet. If they do, add the color of the shot to the respective
sheet's set.
3.
Output: After processing all shots, the size of each sheet’s set will give the
number of unique colors associated with that sheet.
This approach efficiently uses sets to ensure that only unique colors are counted for
each sheet.
3) Card
The problem involved using a greedy approach and working with arrays. While I
can't recall the exact details of the question, it revolved around distributing or sorting
cards in some way that required an optimal solution using a greedy strategy. The
task likely involved finding a way to minimize or maximize certain values based on
the cards' properties (such as their values, positions, or some other attributes).
MCQs - 10 Questions
1.
Blocks of Different Colours Flock Together: This problem involves calculating
the probability of selecting three balls of different colors from a box containing
white, black, and red balls, given certain relationships between the number of
balls of each color.
2.
Printer and Bookshelf Efficiency: This scenario involves a printer and a
bookshelf with various operations like printing papers, stacking books, and
handling failures (paper getting stuck or books falling down), represented by
different operations (X, Y, Z, W).
3.
Binary Tree Check: This question is about the properties of a complete binary
tree, where you need to identify the correct statement related to the structure
and characteristics of a complete binary tree.

HR Question - 1 Question
The question was how I would ensure a smooth transition of responsibilities if I were
leaving a team. Specifically, the question was: "If you are leaving a team, how will you
make sure you communicate all the important details and responsibilities to another
team member?" The focus was on how to effectively transfer knowledge and tasks to
ensure the continuity of the team's work.
Results:
27 people were shortlisted for interviews, and I was one of them. We received the
results on 25 July 2024, in the afternoon.

Interview Round 1: Technical Interview (Duration: 50 minutes)
This round was offline in the TPO Office. I was thinking that the interviewer would start
with my introduction but he told me to not waste the time and start with the interview
directly.
1.
Question on string:
Count the number of unique characters in a given string
Count the number of unique characters in a given String - GeeksforGeeks
Approach:
The first part was straightforward. I suggested using an unordered set to store the
unique characters from the string and returning the size of the set. This approach
would take time complexity of O(n) and a space complexity of O(n).
When they told me to optimize further, I explained using a fixed-size array of 26
elements (for the English alphabet). I traversed the string and incremented the
corresponding index in the array for each character. I maintained a counter variable.
After processing the string, I iterated through the array and increased the counter
when indices with values were greater than zero just once. This reduced the space
complexity to constant.
Follow Up :
Count only those characters in the string whose occurrences are greater than equal
to k in the string
For this part, I stuck to the optimized approach using the fixed-size array of 26
elements. I added a simple condition to check if the value at a specific index was
greater than or equal to k. Only in such cases, I increment the counter variable.
They asked me to write the proper code on the paper.
6

2. Question on Array:
Product of Array except itself
Product of Array except itself - GeeksforGeeks
Since I had already solved this question before, I explained the optimized solution
along with time complexity and space complexity.
Follow up :
1.
There can be 0 as well as negative numbers in the array.
2.
A range of queries was provided, each specifying indices i and j. The task was
to calculate the product of elements within the range [i, j].
3. Question on Stack & Queue:
Data Stream Processing
The interviewer presented a problem involving a continuous data stream of
characters interspersed with integers (1 or 2).
For example: abcdefab1hajvm2....
●
For Characters: Simply print the characters as they appear in the stream.
●
For Integer 1: Backspace or remove the last printed character.
●
For Integer 2: Undo the first deleted character which was recently deleted.
Follow-Up:
We have to undo whatever we deleted first not the recent one.
Approach:
●
I was told to assume any data structure.
7

●
For undoing the most recent deletion, I used a stack, which follows a LIFO (Last
In, First Out) approach.
●
For undoing the first deleted character, I found a queue to be the most optimal
choice due to its FIFO (First In, First Out) nature.
●
The space complexity and time complexity was O(n) and the deletion or
undoing takes place in O(1) time.
4. Question on Linked List:
Continuous Data Stream and Deletion Queries
The problem was about handling a continuous data stream while also processing
queries to delete numbers from the sequence. If the number was present, it had to
be deleted.
Follow-Up:
I had to delete all occurrences of the specified number, as there could be duplicates
in the stream.
My Approach:
I was free to choose any data structure.
I decided to use a doubly linked list, as it allows deletion in O(1) time when you have
a reference to the node. This made it much easier to handle both single and multiple
deletions efficiently.
5. Question on Binary Tree:
The interviewer asked if I was comfortable with binary trees, and I said yes. The
question was:
Given the root of a binary tree, I had to count the total number of nodes at that level
and the number of nodes at each level can be variable or equal.
8

Follow-Up:
Instead of a single level, the query could give a range of levels, and I needed to return
the count of nodes across all levels in that range.
Approach:
For the single-level query, I used a simple level-order traversal (BFS) to count the
nodes at the required level.
For the follow-up, I slightly changed my approach. I added an array to keep track of
the number of nodes at each level while traversing the tree just once. Then, I could
easily sum up the counts for the levels in the given range.
The time complexity and space complexity was the total number of nodes in the tree.
After this question my technical interview ended and I was told to wait outside. In this
round, I was only asked questions related to DSA. After this we had a break for lunch
and after 1 hour one person from the staff came and asked me to go for a second
interview round.
9

Round 2 : HR Round (Duration: 25 - 30 minutes)
1.
How did you come into VJTI? How was your journey? What motivated you to
come here?
I shared my story, explaining that my motivation came from wanting to learn
alongside the brightest minds.
2. What is your favourite subject?
I told him that my favourite subject is Data Structures and Algorithms because
it helps me develop strong problem-solving skills. What I find fascinating
about it is that it’s not just theoretical; the techniques I learn can be directly
applied in real-world projects. For example, when I’m building software or
working on coding challenges, the algorithms I’ve learned come into use,
allowing me to optimize performance, make decisions faster, and handle large
datasets efficiently. I enjoy the process of breaking down complex problems
and finding efficient solutions, which is something DSA has taught me to do
effectively.
3. How will you implement DSA in a real world application? With Examples.
In game development, algorithms like BFS (Breadth-First Search), DFS
(Depth-First Search), and Dijkstra’s algorithm are commonly used to find the
shortest path.
Another example I gave was supply chain management. In this, graph
algorithms can be applied to optimize routes for transporting goods from one
location to another, minimizing time and cost by finding the most efficient
path.
Then I mentioned the use of hashmaps in databases to retrieve data
efficiently. For example, when dealing with large datasets, hashmaps allow us
10

to store data in a way that enables quick retrieval with time complexity O(n) to
O(1) on average, which is essential for applications like querying customer
records in an e-commerce database
.
4. One practical scenario was given of irctc app where millions of people are
booking at same time but seats are only 100 .. so is it a problem because
others people then get tickets as waiting or get refund of their payment but
again it takes minimum 7 working days to return money
At first, I was a bit confused and nervous as I wasn't entirely sure how to
approach the problem. I took a moment to calm myself, and I asked him to
give me time to think, then I asked the interviewer to repeat the question. After
hearing the question again, I thought about how we could improve the
situation.
I explained that we can store timestamp data for each booking and prioritize
the users who have completed their transactions earlier. By implementing this,
we can ensure that seats are allocated based on who booked first, thus
reducing the chances of anyone being unfairly placed on the waiting list.
Next, I proposed improving the system's response time. For example, if seat
updates are currently done in 1 second, reducing this update time to
milliseconds would decrease the number of people affected by delays or
refunds. This would allow the system to handle more transactions efficiently,
which ensures only few people are impacted by the waiting or refund problem.
Then the interviewer asked me if I had any questions to ask then I asked 2 questions
which I had already prepared before.
1.
What kind of problems the current development teams are facing, where we
as an intern can contribute?
11

2.
With the rapid evolution of technology, how does the team stay updated and
adapt to these changes effectively on the existing projects?
With this my second interview ended.
Result:
The results were announced around 4 PM, and 6 students were selected from which I
was the luckiest one.
I honestly couldn’t believe it at first because I had been really nervous. The others in
the room had gone through three rounds of interviews, while I had only done two, so I
was unsure if that would affect my chances. But when my name was called, it was
the moment which I can never forget. It was a huge moment for me, and it felt like all
the hard work had finally paid off.
Key takeaways:
1.
Have a strong hands on at least one programming language. For me, it was
C++.
2.
Coc usually takes mock interviews for those who have actively participated in
the events. These mock interviews are taken by our seniors which have helped
us a lot to prepare before our actual interviews.
3.
Keep Practicing DSA, alongside OOPS, DBMS, CS Fundamentals. Companies
can start coming in the middle of your vacations. So be well prepared.
4. Build a good resume. Take feedback from your seniors. Increase your ATS
Score as much as you can which helps in resume shortlisting.
5. Ensure you mention only the skills and technologies you're genuinely
comfortable with.
6. When you’re confused or nervous, take a deep breath. Don’t be afraid to ask
the interviewer to clarify the question. It shows that you’re thinking carefully
before responding, which is better than rushing into an answer.
12

7.
Always speak out loud while solving DSA problems so the interviewer can
follow your logic and most of the time they give hints if we are not going
towards the correct approach.
8. Bring up edge cases as you go—it shows your thinking capability and how you
solve the problem.
9. While technical skills are important, how you communicate them is equally
important. Explain your thought process clearly and confidently which makes
it easier for interviewers to understand how you approach problems.
10. Read all the interview experiences because maximum time we have the same
format of interview.
Last tip I would like to give you is - Always surround yourself with positive and
supportive people. Coming from a diploma in electronics engineering, the journey
wasn’t easy for me—learning to code, practicing DSA, and balancing academics felt
very exhausting at times. But I was lucky to have amazing friends who constantly
motivated me. Together, we took part in contests, pushing each other to do better
every time. Their encouragement kept me going, and I truly believe that having the
right people around you makes all the difference.
If you have any doubts related to interview prep or the interview experience you can
feel free to reach out to me: snehamenat029@gmail.com . I’ll be happy to help you
as much as I can.
